waves.title: The firing range and your Risen

items.text: The firing range in the Drill Hall, dressed as an old practice yard
Three guns: an auto rifle, a hand cannon and a pulse rifle, with aiming, recoil and reloads
Targets with precision hits and nameplates
A Destiny 2-style HUD: radar, health, Super bar and ammo
Your abilities: sprint, jump, grenade, melee, class ability and a Super, each with its own effects and sounds
The title screen and its music, "Cold Iron"
Choose your kit: Plate, Cloak or Coat
Customise: kind (Human, Exo or Awoken), colours, crest, skin tone, helmet on or off
Kind and body mean something: eye light, skin, build and a wordless voice
Sign in or make an account ("Who's playing?")
Characters saved online, so any device carries on where you left off
More than one Risen on an account, each one saved
Friends added by name, and who's online
Setting out from the fire, with the Survey and the valley map
Fireteams: invite friends to your fire, accept, and set out together
Co-op: friends see each other and fight the same enemies
Your armour shows at the fire, on you and on your friends

waves.title: The opening: three prologues, the Waking and Last Lamps

items.text: Prologue A (Human): the town on the river, the last evening
Prologue B (Exo): the power house, the last night shift
Prologue C (Awoken): the river path near a dead city, the last dusk
Fallen that move, take cover and shoot back: Dregs, a shielded Captain that blinks away, a Servitor
The Waking: your Ghost finds you, centuries later
A second Risen on your account gets a shorter Waking
Last Lamps: the lit quarter, your first Super, and the walk back to the fire
Last Lamps with friends
A waypoint marker, and a Settings screen (field of view, subtitles, damage numbers)

waves.title: The big polish, and the valley opens

items.text: Damage numbers, staggers and proper death falls
Enemies you can read: a Captain's blink winds up first, shields flash when they break
Every gun heard: reports, reloads, hits and footsteps, with muzzle flash, brass and tracers
Armour detail: rivets, straps and pouches, and each piece its own look
The character and abilities screens
The valley in sections, loaded one at a time, with a map on M
Old Angara as open patrol space, with the story's places walkable inside it
A sky that keeps time: a day every 40 minutes, the sun by day and the Moon by night
Bullet impacts that suit each surface, and an Effects detail setting

waves.title: A normal day before each night

items.text: Prologue A by day: the town on the river, the last afternoon
Prologue B by day: the power house, the last shift change
Prologue C by day: the road upriver, with a low root cellar to crouch into
Loading screens: a title card for each prologue, and your Ghost's map with a line from your Ghost
Rooms to walk into: the neighbour's house, the power house's locker room and canteen
Real-looking things: worn, bevelled props, and forests and trees that suit each place
Three simple stats on your armour
One HUD everywhere, with the ammo bottom-left
Guns held properly: a two-handed hand cannon, the prologue rifles in both hands

waves.title: The Far Spans, loot and phones

items.text: The Far Spans: the first walk after the Waking, through Old Angara to a lone fire
Loot: rarities, power and copper
Armour, earned: you wake in what you died in, then find the watch's kit
Each new gun gets a look-over the first time you draw it
Touch controls for phones: a stick to move, drag to look and fire, every mode playable by touch
A tidier map, with fewer patrol points
Travel only to places that are finished
Anonymous crash and play stats, with an off switch in Settings

waves.title: Ready for friends, and First Light

items.text: Gunfeel pass: accuracy, damage falloff, and a sprint you can cancel
Fair, readable fights: enemies give you a moment before their first shot
Team revive, and a new leader if the leader drops
Saved checkpoints in The Far Spans and Last Lamps
The first public event in patrol: the Market Raid
Patrol with friends: Old Angara together, events shared
A Destiny 2-style slide, on X
Old Angara and the Drill Hall draw faster (a speed pass)
First Light, the first strike, for three: the River Works and the power house, and a boss with a health bar

waves.title: Ben's play-test fixes, and the lobby

items.text: Sound back in the Human prologue, with townsfolk murmurs, and the Ghost's constant hum turned off
Believable blockers in the prologues: a collapsed road, overturned carts and crowds, not plain walls
Empty hands until you pick up your first gun
The Ghost's light at night, and mission markers that point the right way
A pause menu in the prologues
The lobby: Play goes to the fire, The Far Spans is played solo until it's done, and checkpoints with Reset on the cards
Rejoin your fireteam after a reload or a drop, even from another device
Walkable wherever it looks walkable: the quay's edge, and no invisible walls at the broken bridge
Admin tools for player saves: look up, reset, grant and unlock (tested offline, not yet used on live saves)

waves.title: Old Angara filled, real voices, and menus

items.text: The Heights filled: a lane of ruined dachas, a chapel, a quarry with its crane, a fallen radio mast
More of Old Angara filled: an old ski slope, terraces on the far bank, a rail yard, and a shrine, a lorry and fishing huts on the Shore road
Four hidden doors placed in Old Angara for lost sectors later (the doors only)
The ground follows the hills as drawn, so you no longer fall through
Fallen patrols and scavengers on the move in patrol
Patrol ambience: Old Angara sounds like a place
Three more public events: Drill in the Works, The Weir and The Water Tank (four in rotation)
Spoken voices in the Human prologue, tuned and placed in the world
The prologue town's clock tower moved out into the square
Settings on the start screens, so you can choose before you load in
A Roadmap button on the menus, showing this checklist
New blocky and smooth bodies to try, behind a setting (Classic stays the default)
The bodies change the moment you pick a new setting
The smooth aiming hand sits properly on the gun (it sits a little low today)
Mouths that move when people talk
Clothes and armour fitted to the new bodies, with real cloth: hoods, long coats, a weave you can see
Walking, crouching and holding poses on the new bodies
More variety in people: faces, hair and builds
The new bodies become the default for everyone
The next sound pass, on the guns
The Ghost's wordless voice changing with its mood
The next effects pass: deaths, abilities, Supers, and your friends' tracers
Weather: mist in the hollows, rain, and snow on the Heights
A pass over the story's words, played through from the start
Every gun given a detail pass: bevelled edges, wear and grime
Every armour piece given a detail pass, by class and rarity
Ben's two-computer co-op test (it decides whether friends on other networks need a relay)
A speed check on the Mac's graphics card, with Ben at the Mac
A test check on enemy timing made reliable (it fails when the Mac is busy)
Publish the online rules from the admin tools, instead of pasting them by hand
The friend picker says why a friend can't join yet ("Hasn't finished The Far Spans")
Reloading in the first seconds of setting out no longer loses your fireteam
Decide what happens to friends when the leader leaves patrol for the fire
Co-op still to prove: First Light together, and three players in one activity
Switch on the online service's extra protection (set up, not switched on yet)
The Fire as a place you can walk around, built in Gatefire
People at the fires: refugees, a lamp-keeper, a quartermaster's table, children and a dog
Townsfolk and refugees on the roads, who run when the Fallen come near
Gatefire's empty ground filled: the old wall's lost stretch, a boathouse and jetty, a work camp by the tunnel, abandoned carts, a salvage yard
The camp's own sounds
More kinds of gun: scout rifle, sub-machine gun, sidearm, shotgun, sniper rifle, fusion rifle and rocket launcher
Heavy ammo
Perks and random rolls on guns
XP and levels
Traders at The Fire
Bounties, and a quest tracker
A vault for spare gear, collections and triumphs
Gamepad support
Jumps and slides that feel the same at any frame rate
Doors that open in Old Angara: a bakery, a school, a church crypt stair, a station waiting room
The first lost sector: the Crypt, a short dungeon with a boss and a chest
The other three lost sectors: the Pump Room, the Cistern and the Cellars
Patrol beacons: small jobs to pick up in patrol
Small encounters between places: a refugee to escort, a supply drop, a Shank swarm at dusk
Wildlife: crows that lift as you pass, deer, herons, a fox
The Diggings, the Tithe Marches and the Spillway filled, each ahead of its missions
The Floodmeadow, the High Woods, the Farmsteads and the Shore Line filled
A public event, Fallen patrols, townsfolk and sound in every section

waves.title: The story goes on: strikes, The Lists and the raid

items.text: The rest of Act 1
Act 2 of the story
Act 3, and the Epilogue
The Fire grows as the story goes on
More strikes: four in all to start, six by the end
The Lists, PvP for friends: Duel (1 v 1) and Three Stones (3 v 3), guns only at first
The Lists, later: abilities and Supers, a 2 v 2 mode, and a six-player free-for-all
A six-player network test, then the raid
Expansions: a smaller one first, along the road west, then the Moon as the big one
